del10.py.summary: Delete the lines of a file that are shorter than a minimum length.
details: Every line whose stripped text is shorter than the threshold (10 characters by default) is dropped and the file is rewritten in place.

delafter.py.summary: Cut each line of a file at the first occurrence of a marker character.
details: Keeps the text before the marker (the marker itself is dropped), leaves lines without it untouched and drops empty lines before rewriting the file in place.

delbefor.py.summary: Cut each line of a file after the first occurrence of a marker character.
details: Keeps everything after the marker, leaves lines without it untouched and drops empty lines before rewriting the file in place.

delshort.py.summary: Delete tiny text files below the current directory.
details: Binary files are skipped; a text file is removed when it is under 100 bytes or has fewer than three lines, which clears placeholder and accidental files.

deob.py.summary: Deobfuscate a bash script whose commands are assembled from variables and ``eval``.
details: Parses the string assignments in the file, substitutes the variables into the ``eval`` string, removes the escape noise and prints (or writes with ``-o``) the readable script. Variables that cannot be resolved are reported instead of guessed.

detect_encoding.py.summary: Compare what several encoding detectors think the local text files use.
details: Runs chardet, charset_normalizer, cchardet, BeautifulSoup's UnicodeDammit, libmagic and the standard ``tokenize``/BOM heuristics (each one only when installed) over the files below the current directory and prints the guesses side by side, flagging files where the detectors disagree.

distinfo.py.summary: List the packages that are installed with more than one version.
details: Reads the ``.dist-info``/``.egg-info`` directory names of every ``site-packages`` location and prints the packages whose name appears with several versions, so leftovers from earlier installs become visible.

distinfo2.py.summary: Trim ``.dist-info`` directories down to the standard metadata files.
details: Keeps ``METADATA``, ``RECORD``, ``WHEEL`` and ``top_level.txt`` and removes the extra files that packagers leave behind (``INSTALLER``, ``REQUESTED``, ``direct_url.json``, license and author files, ``LICENSE`` copies ...).

dj.py.summary: Delete junk files from directories that are not under version control.
details: Reads extra junk names from ``/sdcard/data/junk``, combines them with the built-in suffix list (``.pyc``, ``.tmp``, ``.log``, ``.bak``, ``.exe``, ``.dll`` ...) and removes matching files and caches. Git metadata (``.gitignore``, ``.gitkeep``, ``.github``) is preserved and nothing is touched inside a repository unless the rules allow it.

dj2.py.summary: Remove ``.github`` folders and ``.gitignore`` files from a directory that is not a git repository.
details: Aborts when the current directory is a repository, otherwise it walks the tree and deletes leftover git metadata files and folders, reporting every removal.

dll.py.summary: Delete a range of lines from a file.
details: Without an end line everything from the start line to the end of the file is removed; line numbers are one-based and the file is rewritten in place, printing how many lines remained.
Copies the given file into ``/sdcard/doc`` (creating the directory when needed) and deletes the original; an existing destination aborts the move instead of overwriting.

docstring_formatter.py.summary: Reflow the module docstring bodies of Python files to 80 columns.
details: Splits the docstring body into sentences and list items, re-wraps the prose to ``MAX_LINE`` and writes the file back only when the text actually changes. String prefixes are preserved and only module docstrings are rewritten, not the function docstrings.

dos2utf-8.py.summary: Re-encode every text file below the current directory as UTF-8 with LF line endings.
details: Walks plain files and the members of the archives it can open (through ``archive_walker``), skips binary data (NUL bytes), decodes as UTF-8 with a Latin-1 fallback, normalizes CRLF/CR to LF and writes the file back only when something changed.
